html:
In 1690 tens of thousands of Serbs left Ottoman lands in Kosovo and southern Serbia and moved north into Habsburg Hungary. The exact number is disputed.

It happened during the Great Turkish War. After the Ottomans failed to take Vienna in 1683, Habsburg armies pushed deep into the Balkans, and many Serbs rose to help them. Then the Ottomans struck back. Fearing reprisals, Serbs fled with the retreating army, led by their patriarch Arsenije III Čarnojević.

Emperor Leopold I granted them privileges: their own church and freedom of worship. They settled along the Danube, in today's Vojvodina and around Buda, and many served as soldiers on the Military Frontier against the Ottomans. Their church centre moved to Sremski Karlovci. Another wave followed in the 1730s. Kosovo, left emptier, slowly gained more Albanian settlers, a change still argued over today.
sum: In 1690 tens of thousands of Serbs left Ottoman lands in Kosovo and southern Serbia and moved north into Habsburg Hungary. The exact number is disputed.
